nodes.summary: The Bernoulli(`p`) product weight: every coordinate is `true` with probability `p`.
nodes.title: Bernoulli product weight

nodes.summary: Root step of the OSSS induction: the covariance of a function whose discrete derivative in `e` is bounded by `1` with the martingale increment `g - 𝔼[g | ω_{≠e}]` is at most `Infₑ(g)`.
nodes.title: Root step of the OSSS induction

nodes.summary: Subtree step of the OSSS induction: for `G` independent of the root variable `e`, the covariance with a tree rooted at `e` splits into the covariances with the two subtrees under the conditioned weights.
nodes.title: Subtree step of the OSSS induction

nodes.summary: The conditional expectation of `g` given all coordinates except `e`.
nodes.title: Conditional expectation given the other coordinates

nodes.summary: The covariance `𝔼[f g] - 𝔼[f] 𝔼[g]` under the product weight `ν`.
nodes.title: Covariance under a product weight

nodes.summary: A binary decision tree on the variables `E`: a leaf outputs a Boolean value, and a node queries a variable and continues in the first subtree if it is `true` and in the second otherwise.
nodes.title: Binary decision tree

nodes.summary: The function computed by the decision tree, as a `0/1`-valued real function.
nodes.title: Real-valued function computed by a decision tree

nodes.summary: The Boolean function computed by the decision tree.
nodes.title: Boolean function computed by a decision tree

nodes.summary: The Bernoulli(`p`) product weight computes integrals against `StatMech.bernoulliProductMeasure`, the corresponding product probability measure.
nodes.title: Bernoulli product weight computes product-measure integrals

nodes.summary: The expectation `∑_ω weight ν ω * g ω` of `g` under the product weight `ν`.
nodes.title: Expectation under a product weight

nodes.summary: The configuration `ω` with coordinate `e` flipped.
nodes.title: Configuration with one coordinate flipped

nodes.summary: The decision tree that queries every variable and then outputs the value of `φ`; it computes `φ` and has revealment `1` at every variable.
nodes.title: Decision tree querying every variable

nodes.summary: The decision tree that queries the variables of `l` in order and then outputs the value of `φ` at the configuration that agrees with the answers on `l` and is `false` elsewhere. It computes `φ` when `φ` depends only on the variables in `l` (`eval_fullTree`).
nodes.title: Decision tree querying a list of variables

nodes.summary: The influence of `e` on the indicator of `A` is the probability that `e` is pivotal for `A`.
nodes.title: Influence on an indicator is the pivotal probability

nodes.summary: The influence of coordinate `e` on `g`: `𝔼 |g(ω^{e ↦ 1}) - g(ω^{e ↦ 0})|`. For the indicator of an event this is the probability that `e` is pivotal (`infl_indicator_eq_pivotal`).
nodes.title: Influence of a coordinate

nodes.summary: `φ` depends only on the coordinates in the list `l`.
nodes.title: Function depending only on listed coordinates

nodes.summary: `ν` is a product probability weight: each `ν e` is a probability vector on `Bool`.
nodes.title: Product probability weight

nodes.summary: The OSSS inequality for the Bernoulli(`p`) product measure.
nodes.title: OSSS inequality for the Bernoulli product measure

nodes.summary: The OSSS covariance inequality, stated for all product weights at once so that it can be proved by induction on the decision tree. Use `osss` for the usual argument order.
nodes.title: OSSS covariance inequality over all product weights

nodes.summary: OSSS inequality (O'Donnell, Saks, Schramm, Servedio, *Every decision tree has an influential variable*, FOCS 2005): if the decision tree `T` computes `f`, then `Var(f) ≤ ∑ᵢ δᵢ(T) Infᵢ(f)` under every product probability measure.
nodes.title: OSSS inequality

nodes.summary: OSSS inequality, covariance form (O'Donnell, Saks, Schramm, Servedio, *Every decision tree has an influential variable*, FOCS 2005; in this form Duminil-Copin, Raoufi, Tassion, Ann. of Math. 2019): if the decision tree `T` computes the Boolean function `f`, then for every real function `g` and every product probability measure, `Cov(f, g) ≤ ∑ᵢ δᵢ(T) Infᵢ(g)`, where `Infᵢ(g) = 𝔼 |g(ω^{i ↦ 1}) - g(ω^{i ↦ 0})|`.
nodes.title: OSSS inequality

nodes.summary: `poincare` for the Bernoulli(`p`) product measure.
nodes.title: Poincaré inequality for the Bernoulli product measure

nodes.summary: Covariance form of `poincare`: `Cov(1_A, g) ≤ ∑ₑ Infₑ(g)` for every real function `g`.
nodes.title: Covariance form of the Poincaré inequality

nodes.summary: Poincaré inequality for Boolean functions under a product measure: `Var(1_A) ≤ ∑ₑ Infₑ(1_A)`, where `Infₑ(1_A)` is the probability that `e` is pivotal. This is the OSSS inequality for the full decision tree; it is weaker than the Efron–Stein inequality `Var(f) ≤ ∑ₑ pₑ(1 - pₑ) 𝔼[(∂ₑ f)²]` by the factor `pₑ(1 - pₑ) ≤ 1/4`.
nodes.title: Poincaré inequality for Boolean functions under a product measure

nodes.summary: The point mass at `b`, as a weight on `Bool`. Replacing `ν e` by `pt b` conditions on `ω e = b`.
nodes.title: Point-mass weight on the Booleans

nodes.summary: The set of variables the decision tree queries on input `ω`.
nodes.title: Variables queried by a decision tree on an input

nodes.summary: The revealment `δₑ(T)`: the probability that the decision tree `T` queries the variable `e`.
nodes.title: Revealment of a variable by a decision tree

nodes.summary: The variance of `g` under the product weight `ν`.
nodes.title: Variance under a product weight

nodes.summary: The probability `∏ₑ ν e (ω e)` of the configuration `ω` under the product weight `ν`.
nodes.title: Probability of a configuration under a product weight

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
